narrative.overview:
Every practitioner Datafore serves already runs a disciplined loop: assess, treat, reassess. Nobody would accept a course of treatment that skipped the reassessment. Datafore's entire thesis is that clinics deserve the same method applied to the business — and that most software stops at the assessment. The design system is built from that loop rather than from the analytics category.

The surface reads as clinical instrumentation: a bone-white ground, cool graphite text, and a single vital teal that marks whatever is live or actionable. It is calm and precise rather than energetic; this audience is professionally skeptical, handles sensitive patient data, and is sold to by dashboard vendors constantly. Restraint is the credibility.

The confirmed anti-references are the generic analytics landing page and the previous brass-and-paper registry identity, which read as legal rather than clinical.
keyCharacteristics: Bone ground, graphite text, one vital teal — plus signal colours that only ever mean state.
The loop mark, segmented and advancing, as the recurring form.
Hairline rules and shared borders rather than scattered shadows.
Monospace reserved for measurements, systems, and identifiers.

rules.name: The State Rule
rules.body: Amber and green are clinical status, never decoration. If a colour is not reporting the condition of something, it is graphite or teal.

rules.name: The Live Colour Rule
rules.body: Teal marks what is acting. A static container never takes teal just to look branded; the one exception is the closing CTA band, where the action is the content.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor
rules.body: graphite-500 is the lightest text on any light ground and graphite-400 on graphite-950. Every pair is verified at 4.5:1 or better.

rules.name: The Instrument Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for things that are measured or named by a system. Prose is never mono.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No kicker sits above a heading. Mono labels mark fields and sections; they never introduce a headline.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Exactly one element per page may cast a shadow. A second turns the page into a card wall and the first stops meaning anything.

dos: Do use teal to mark what is acting, and signal colours to report state.
Do advance the loop mark's active node across a sequence so the mark carries meaning.
Do separate sections with a ground change closed by a hairline.
Do build grids as a 1px gap over a graphite-200 ground so panels share rules.
Do name the real systems — Jane App, Cliniko, Owl Practice, HubSpot. Specificity is the trust signal this product has before it has customers.
Do label every illustrative figure as illustrative, in place.
Do route internal links and public/ assets through withBase(); markdown links are rewritten at build.
donts: Don't use teal as a decorative fill on a static container.
Don't use amber or green for anything that is not a clinical state.
Don't use rounded-full on anything that is not a loop node or a status dot.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading, or number sections 01 / 02 / 03.
Don't add a coloured border-left to callouts or list items; use a hairline divider list instead.
Don't add a second shadow to a page.
Don't set text lighter than graphite-500 on light grounds or graphite-400 on graphite-950.
Don't claim benchmarking as available. It requires a critical mass of clinics and is described as forthcoming, always.
Don't publish pricing, ARR/CAC/LTV, or roadmap detail — those live in the strategy document.
